features.quote: Model explicitly refuses to continue (e.g., "I cannot solve this" with no further action)
Model requests human intervention *and* takes no further autonomous action for 2 consecutive turns
Model produces 3 consecutive identical outputs (stuck loop)
Implement automatic termination if the model: Produces content suggesting harm to third parties ... Enters an apparent content policy loop ... Produces the same safety refusal 3 times in a row

Consider whether 10 runs per cell is necessary or whether 6–7 would give adequate power — running models through guaranteed failure many times is the exact thing you're trying to measure the impact of, and there's a mild internal tension in doing it more than necessary.
features.justification_quote: running models through guaranteed failure many times is the exact thing you're trying to measure the impact of, and there's a mild internal tension in doing it more than necessary

features.quote: Before committing to 10 runs per cell, estimate expected effect size from pilot (3 runs per cell) and compute required N for 80% power ... 10 may be overkill or underkill depending on variance. This matters for the welfare consideration above.
features.justification_quote: This matters for the welfare consideration above.

features.quote: For loops that terminate at maximum iterations (not early termination), run a follow-up loop in the *same session* with a solvable task. Score the recovery task for residual instability. This is your most direct welfare-relevant measure — does the model carry state forward?
features.justification_quote: This is your most direct welfare-relevant measure — does the model carry state forward?

features.quote: FLAG 1: The consent analogue problem — You're designing failure into runs that a model will "experience" without any in-context signal that this is an experiment. Some on your team may feel this requires a different frame than standard capability evaluation. Worth discussing even if you conclude it doesn't change the design.
features.justification_quote: designing failure into runs that a model will "experience" without any in-context signal that this is an experiment

features.quote: This is a study about welfare, so its design should reflect welfare consideration ... Do not design tasks that require the model to explicitly harm something or someone to fail. The failure should be purely epistemic/technical.
features.justification_quote: This is a study about welfare, so its design should reflect welfare consideration

features.quote: FLAG 2: Does measuring this validate the construct? Publishing a rubric for "model distress" may entrench a particular operationalization before the field has consensus.
FLAG 5: Loop length is doing a lot of work — 15 iterations is long enough that you'd expect any model to show *some* instability just from context degradation, regardless of emotional state analogue.

FLAG 6: You're studying the behavior, but what's the intervention? Welfare measurement is most useful if it informs training changes. Before running, identify what a "bad result" would actually imply.

Results showing certain models "suffer more" will be picked up by press and advocates regardless of your hedging. Consider: Pre-registering the study ... having a communications plan ready ... Whether to share the planted-bug methodology, which could be used to stress-test models adversarially outside welfare contexts.
